ca_hippo_wall.blurb: A compact slab wall within Tollhouse Rock, in the Sierra foothills east of Fresno along Highway 168. It holds ten routes, nearly all of them bolted with a single gear-protected line, and the grades sit between 5.7 and 5.9, with most at 5.8. That makes it a friendly spot for newer leaders. Lines run roughly 25 to 38 metres, long for a slab wall, so check your rope length and bring about a dozen quickdraws. Anchors at the top are doubled for lowering or rappelling. It is a good companion to the bigger multi-pitch lines on the main dome nearby.
ca_hippo_wall.approach: From the slab where the rough road ends, follow the descent trail down the gully and keep right. Hippo Wall is the lower sport slab on your right; a small trail splits off the main descent path and runs along its base.

ca_left_side_2.blurb: The first wall you meet on the trail into Rainbow, a small roadside crag beside Interstate 80 near Big Bend in the Lake Tahoe region, at about 5,900 feet. Ten routes, mostly trad with a couple of bolted lines and one winter ice or mixed line. Grades run from 5.8 up through the low 5.12s, and the wall holds several of the hardest lines at Rainbow along with a few classics. It sees little traffic despite the freeway proximity, but it is not a beginner venue; the middle and upper grades dominate.

ca_left_side_3.blurb: The taller, more featured left-hand portion of 8000 Foot Crag, alongside Highway 38 in the San Bernardino Mountains at roughly 8,100 feet. Ten routes, nine of them bolted sport and one trad, ranging from a 5.4 up to 5.11, with the bulk in the 5.10 range. The rock is broken-looking but solid. Many lines are newer and lightly travelled, so expect some dirt on holds. The crag is cool in warm weather, since it is shaded by its northerly exposure and holds snow near the base into early summer, and it makes a handy stop on the drive to or from Big Bear.

ca_main_wall_center.blurb: A short stretch of Squarenail, the mostly-sport crag near Tollhouse and Shaver Lake off Highway 168 in the southern Sierra foothills, at roughly 3,100 feet. Ten climbs, seven bolted and three trad, with thin, technical slab climbing as the main flavour. Grades run from a 5.4 to the low 5.12s, but most fall in the 5.10 to 5.11 range, so it suits climbers comfortable on steady slab. Routes are reached from Playground Ledge, where a rappel station at the far end drops to the ledge below. The same ledge is a quick way across to the Main Wall - Right lines.

ca_motown.blurb: A sport sector at Mickey's Beach, in Marin County near Stinson Beach on the coast. Nearly all the climbing here is on the sand, and some of it depends on the tide, so check conditions before walking down. The area is known for some of the hardest bolted routes around San Francisco, and it can be windy. Motown holds ten routes, nine bolted and one trad, with grades from 5.10 to 5.12. Most sit at 5.11, so it suits climbers already comfortable on steep, sustained sport lines rather than beginners.

ca_isles_corridor_left_side.blurb: The west side of a hidden corridor tucked behind the Isles in the Sky wall, in the Split Rocks part of Joshua Tree National Park's Pinto Basin, at about 4,400 feet. Ten trad routes, mostly cracks with a few face climbs. Grades run from an easy 5.2 up to the low 5.11s, with a cluster at 5.9 and 5.10 that includes the corridor's best-known crack lines. An easy crack at the entrance doubles as the way back down. Bring a standard rack with extra small to medium cams for the finger and hand cracks.
ca_isles_corridor_left_side.approach: Hike as for the Isles in the Sky wall, aiming for the left end of the face. Walk around its left side, then scramble over blocks to enter the corridor.
